description: Route-level bundle size budgets for authenticated Next.js pages. Budgets cover the First Load JS (shared chunks + page chunk) for each route segment. Values are in bytes. Measured values are filled by the post-build bundle analyzer and compared against the declared ceiling by the orchestrator. A null measured value means the route has not been profiled yet.

network.mobile: ~1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 150ms RTT — close to Fast 3G+ (frontend/scripts/measure-web-vitals.mjs MOBILE_PROFILE: 1,600,000/8 bytes/s down, 750,000/8 bytes/s up, 150ms latency)

cpu.mobile: 4x CPU slowdown (Chrome DevTools mid-tier mobile preset)

referenceProfile.notes: Measured by frontend/scripts/measure-web-vitals.mjs, which drives a headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol against `next build && next start`; the earlier claim that these came from Lighthouse 12 in CI was not true of anything in this repository. Field data (CrUX) is the source of truth for production; lab data here is the gating proxy. The 100ms responsiveness rule (CLAUDE.md section 12.2) is enforced by INP <= 200ms and measured directly as perceivedResponsiveness in the capture. measuredFirstLoadJsBytes is gzip(9) summed over the unique chunks in each route's page_client-reference-manifest.js from a production build, and measuredPageChunkBytes is the additive over the /dashboard baseline — both produced by scripts/measure-route-bundles.mjs. measuredScriptBytes, measuredCssBytes, measuredImageBytes, measuredFontBytes, measuredThirdPartyBytes, measuredServerPayloadBytes and measuredTotalBytes are over-the-wire encoded bytes from a cold-cache navigation, produced by measure-web-vitals.mjs. measuredScriptBytes is roughly twice measuredFirstLoadJsBytes on this app because hydration fetches chunks the client-reference manifest does not list.

budgetExceptions.owner: streamlineos-backend — GET /me/access, plus ticket 28 for the frontend seam that issues it
budgetExceptions.reason: Authenticated TTFB is one backend round trip per server render, not a page cost. lib/rbac/get-server-access.ts issues GET /me/access on every authenticated render (React cache() dedupes within a render, never across them); measured on this machine against the same backend, p50 503 ms / max 1004 ms, with POST /auth/session-exchange at p50 563 ms and GET /auth/session-data at p50 100 ms. The same production server returns the public landing in 9-13 ms TTFB, so no part of this number is bundle, route composition or render. Desktop applies no network emulation, so its TTFB is the server render alone.
budgetExceptions.evidence: 192-sample authenticated production capture, build id qlh_3k7hMskrlYGND5MMp, 12 routes x 2 profiles x 8 repetitions, 0 unauthorized and 0 off-route samples

budgetExceptions.owner: streamlineos-backend — GET /me/access, plus ticket 28 for the frontend seam that issues it
budgetExceptions.reason: Same cause as the desktop TTFB exception. The mobile profile adds 150 ms of emulated RTT, which accounts for roughly a sixth of the 932 ms p95 and not for the breach.
budgetExceptions.evidence: same capture; unthrottled server-side Node fetch to first byte over the same 12 routes measured p50 500-602 ms, p95 569-1218 ms, all HTTP 200

budgetExceptionsNote: An exception records who owns a breach and why. It is annotation only: check-web-vitals-budget.mjs prints it next to the failure and still exits non-zero, and its self-test asserts that an exception never reduces the failure count. Nothing here makes a red budget green.
notes: Vitals figures come from frontend/scripts/measure-web-vitals.mjs driving Chrome over CDP against a production `next build` + `next start`, with a minted NextAuth session cookie; nothing here runs Lighthouse and no CI job produces these numbers. Byte figures are a separate cache-disabled first-load pass: measuredFirstLoadJsBytes is gzip over the route's client-reference manifest, measuredScriptBytes and measuredTotalBytes are what the browser actually downloaded before the load event, and measuredPostLoadScriptBytes is the shell's speculative tail recorded beside the route rather than charged to it.

measurementNotes.measurementProvenance2026_09_03: MIXED PROVENANCE — read this before citing a number; three builds are represented and each field says which. (1) measuredFirstLoadJsBytes and measuredPageChunkBytes on all 13 routes are from production build 5WVxD_Jbi032lOZ_Z0NdN (NEXTAUTH_SECRET=<49-char local placeholder> NODE_ENV=production npx next build, exit 0, 601 routes, 2026-09-03), written by node scripts/measure-route-bundles.mjs --write. (2) measuredScriptBytes, measuredTotalBytes, measuredCssBytes, measuredImageBytes, measuredFontBytes, measuredThirdPartyBytes, measuredServerPayloadBytes and the measuredPostLoad* pair are STILL from the 2026-09-02 browser cold-cache capture on build 5KxS0uW9Wrm0BIVYZicTs. Those over-the-wire figures now KNOWINGLY OVERSTATE: they predate the @animateicons tree-shaking fix, which removed a measured 41,613 B gzip from a chunk in the first load of 559 of 601 routes and moved every route's measuredFirstLoadJsBytes down by 36,103–36,660 B gzip. They are left in place rather than adjusted because an estimate is not a measurement — nulling them would also silently drop 14 breaches from the gate. (3) The intermediate build pRoNmQpD1X5_6lTUEhSv9 (2026-09-03) is no longer cited by any field; it is the pre-fix control and appears only in the notes. WHAT IS NOT RUN: no browser cold-cache pass exists for 5WVxD_Jbi032lOZ_Z0NdN. Blocker, stated so it can be routed: the only backend running on this machine (scratch_t30_browser, port 1501, another lane's process) answers CORS for http://localhost:1000 and http://localhost:3000 only, both ports are held by other agents' servers, and the repo .env points NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL at :1500 where nothing listens — so an authenticated capture needs either another lane's port or a restart of another lane's backend.
measurementNotes.sharedShellComposition2026_09_03: Measured on build pRoNmQpD1X5_6lTUEhSv9 from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json plus gzip(9) over the chunk files. /dashboard first load by Next own accounting: 2,281,422 B raw / 573,428 B gzip over 42 chunks — the 441,834 B recorded as measuredFirstLoadJsBytes is the client-reference-manifest subset (37 chunks) and excludes framework/polyfill/main. The two largest identifiable libraries in that shell: (1) @animateicons/react/lucide — chunk 448xe3n3zsx8s.js, 481,691 B raw / 55,869 B gzip, first load of 559 of 601 routes; (2) framer-motion 12.23.25 — chunk 2-tfck0qpw5kq.js, 95,216 B raw / 30,554 B gzip (one merged module of 94,837 B), first load of 601 of 601 routes. The icon library is the larger of the two and had never been recorded.
measurementNotes.framerMotionScope2026_09_03: framer-motion has 278 importers at head: 22 in features/landing, 256 authenticated (hr 46, build 42, app/(authenticated) 27, crm 23, org-setup 15, notifications 14, payroll 10, then a tail). Used API surface: motion (256 files), useReducedMotion (102), AnimatePresence (67), then single-digit LayoutGroup / MotionConfig / useTransform / useSpring / useMotionValue / useInView. WHAT REMOVING IT WOULD ACTUALLY SAVE, measured by bundling the used surface in isolation with the repo esbuild 0.27.1 (--bundle --minify --format=esm, react external): full used surface 121,284 B raw / 40,690 B gzip; motion + AnimatePresence + useReducedMotion 117,537 B raw / 39,330 B gzip; useReducedMotion ALONE 368 B raw / 253 B gzip. The 102 useReducedMotion-only sites are therefore free and the entire price is motion/AnimatePresence. Upper bound on the saving: about 40 kB gzip off every first load, against 17 breaches whose SMALLEST overage is 59,598 B. Replacing framer-motion does not close the JS budget on its own, and it is not the largest thing in the shell.
measurementNotes.animateIconsFinding2026_09_03: SUPERSEDED BY animateIconsFixed2026_09_03 — kept for the diagnosis. NOT TREE-SHAKEN, AND THE CONFIGURED OPTIMISATION IS VACUOUS. @animateicons/react/lucide 0.3.4 ships all 248 animated icons into the first load of 559 of 601 routes while the app imports only 90 distinct icons across 596 files — verified by counting displayName= literals in the built chunk (248) against the import sites (90). next.config.ts ALREADY lists @animateicons/react/lucide in experimental.optimizePackageImports and it cannot bite: the package is one 412,078 B ESM file (dist/lucide.js) with no per-icon modules for a barrel rewrite to target, and it carries ZERO @__PURE__ annotations on 248 top-level forwardRef(...) calls, so no bundler is permitted to drop an unused one. Reproduced outside Next with esbuild: re-exporting all 248 gives 455,497 B raw / 60,394 B gzip, re-exporting only the 90 used gives 452,184 B raw / 59,354 B gzip — a 1,040 B difference. It is structurally unshakeable, not mis-configured. It also VENDORS ITS OWN COPY of framer-motion (dist/chunk-SZP4YRB3.js, 73,833 B, carrying transformPerspective / anticipate / whileHover / originX) while declaring no dependency on it, so framer-motion ships TWICE in every authenticated first load. Prorating 90/248 of the gzip figure puts roughly 35 kB gzip per first load in unused icons. OWNER: not ticket 26 — this is a dependency decision, and it is a larger lever than framer-motion.
measurementNotes.totalBytesBudgetHonesty2026_09_03: defaults.maxTotalBytes = 1,048,576 B is GOVERNED — check-route-bundle-budget compares measuredTotalBytes against it and the self-test asserts that pair fires — but it is LOOSE. On the 2026-09-02 capture all 13 routes were inside it; closest were /chat 989,423 B (94.4%), /build/my-work 963,374 (91.9%), /crm/leads 951,954 (90.8%). It would fire, but it has never rejected anything and it sits above a measuredScriptBytes ceiling that 14 of the same routes breach, so it must not be cited as evidence that page weight is under control. STILL DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED 2026-09-03: those measuredTotalBytes figures predate the @animateicons fix and no browser pass has re-measured them, so any new ceiling set today would be fitted to numbers that are known to be wrong. THE RIGHT NUMBER, stated so the decision can be made rather than deferred again: derive it from the component ceilings this manifest already enforces instead of from the measured maximum. maxScriptBytes 524,288 + maxCssBytes 65,536 + maxFontBytes 131,072 + the measured image range (2,907–14,480, against a 16,384 per-route ceiling on the routes that set one) + maxThirdPartyBytes 0 as actually measured gives about 737,280 B (720 KiB). That is the value maxTotalBytes should take, because at 1,048,576 a route can meet every component budget and still have 311 kB of unattributed headroom, which is what makes the total budget unable to reject anything. Adopt 737,280 in the SAME change that brings measuredScriptBytes inside 524,288 — adopting it before then manufactures a second red field on routes already red for JS, and the gate stops distinguishing the two problems.
measurementNotes.orgSwitcherDynamicImport2026_09_03: SETTLED. components/layout/header/org-switcher.tsx imported @/features/settings/organization/leave-organization-control twice — statically for LeaveOrganizationMenuItem and through next/dynamic for LeaveOrganizationDialog. The dynamic() deferred NOTHING: on build pRoNmQpD1X5_6lTUEhSv9 the dialog own description string sits in .next/static/chunks/176qxkejwz55m.js (71,974 B raw / 22,373 B gzip) together with the menu item, and that chunk is a FIRST-LOAD chunk of 556 of 601 routes (checked directly against /dashboard, /inbox and /settings). No async chunk carrying the module exists anywhere under .next/static/chunks — the only other file containing the string is 1-t3ze_xbo39w.js, itself a first-load chunk of /settings/organization. The dynamic() was collapsed to a static import. Byte saving: zero; the value is that the construct no longer claims a deferral it never performed. Dropping ssr:false is safe because the dialog returns null unless access.isOrgOwner === false and ConfirmDialog renders through a Radix portal that emits nothing while closed.
measurementNotes.animateIconsFixed2026_09_03: FIXED 2026-09-03, measured on two production builds. The package is patched through pnpm (frontend/patches/@animateicons__react@0.3.4.patch, declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml patchedDependencies) so that (a) every one of the 248 top-level `var X=forwardRef(...)` declarations in dist/lucide.js carries /*#__PURE__*/ and the immediately-following `X.displayName="…"` is folded into a PURE Object.assign, making each icon a single droppable expression while keeping the DevTools name, and (b) dist/chunk-SZP4YRB3.js — the 73,833 B copy of motion@12 the package inlined while declaring no dependency on it — is replaced by a three-line re-export of the framer-motion 12.23.25 the app already ships (LazyMotion/m/domMin/useReducedMotion/useAnimation plus a className joiner). pnpm-workspace.yaml packageExtensions declares that dependency edge so resolution does not rest on hoisting. MEASURED. Pre-fix build pRoNmQpD1X5_6lTUEhSv9: chunk 448xe3n3zsx8s.js, 481,691 B raw / 55,886 B gzip, 248 icon displayName literals, first load of 559 of 601 routes. Post-fix build 5WVxD_Jbi032lOZ_Z0NdN: chunk 1_nkc_jwewkee.js, 147,629 B raw / 14,273 B gzip, exactly 90 icon displayName literals — the 90 the app imports, and 90 is also the total across every chunk in .next/static/chunks. Delta -334,062 B raw / -41,613 B gzip. Chunks containing framer-motion's transformPerspective marker went 3 -> 2. measuredFirstLoadJsBytes fell on all 13 governed routes by 36,103–36,660 B gzip (baseline /dashboard 441,834 -> 405,502, -8.2%), and the three measuredFirstLoadJsBytes breaches shrank from +109,462/+73,324/+63,798 to +72,802/+37,206/+27,657 — 246,584 B of overage down to 137,665 B. ALSO PROVED VACUOUS: build 5WVxD_Jbi032lOZ_Z0NdN removed "@animateicons/react", "@animateicons/react/lucide" and "@animateicons/react/huge" from experimental.optimizePackageImports and the icon chunk came out byte-identical (147,629 / 14,273) with every route within ±32 B except /calendar at +696 B of chunk-splitting noise. The entries were removed. NOT DONE: the app still ships 90 animated icons whose animation is real product behaviour — hooks/common/use-animated-icon.ts drives startAnimation on hover at 323 of 412 call sites — so swapping them for plain lucide-react is a design decision, not a bundle fix, and was not made here.
